dimension_1_problem_framing.text: The paper tackles phishing detection as a major cyber threat that causes monetary loss, reputational damage, and business disruption, emphasizing that many organizations still lack sufficient technology to identify bogus URLs and that traditional blocklist-based detection struggles with evolving techniques such as DGAs. It frames a broader research gap as the shortage of comprehensive phishing models that jointly consider multiple elements of phishing schemes, while this work focuses primarily on URL and webpage-code–based detection within that wider context.

dimension_2_quantum_method.text: The core classifier is a shallow hybrid quantum-classical convolutional neural network (SHQCNN) that, according to the authors, combines advantages of classical and quantum computing, using a variational quantum circuit (VQC) to reduce parameters and operate in the NISQ regime. The variational quantum algorithm (VQA) is described as combining kernel encoding and multiple output methods to support effective multi-class classification, with kernel coding claimed to lower computational complexity and improve feature separability. However, the authors explicitly state that no real quantum experiment was carried out: the quantum component is simulated using classical frameworks rather than executed on quantum hardware.

dimension_3_key_results.text: Across four public phishing URL datasets, the proposed OptSHQCNN framework reportedly achieves very high performance, with overall accuracy, precision, recall, and F1/FI-score values above 99% and MCC around 99%, and false positive rates well below 1%. Detailed results show accuracies of 99.36% on Mendeley_2020, 99.18% on ISCX-URL-2016, 99.12% on a URL-based dataset, and 99.17% on PhishStorm, alongside low computational time (around 9–13 ms) in feature selection and optimization. The authors also report that kernel coding improves phishing classification by reducing computational complexity and that an optimizer configuration using their shuffled shepherd algorithm yields the best accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score among tested optimizers.

dimension_4_classical_comparison.text: The study claims that the proposed OptSHQCNN-based method outperforms a range of popular phishing detection and optimization methods, including traditional machine learning (e.g., Random Forest), deep learning variants (e.g., DNN+LSTM), and standard optimizers. On each benchmark dataset, the authors report that their model achieves the best performance across accuracy, precision, recall, F1/FI-score, and MCC compared to these classical baselines, and they further highlight that their custom optimizer configuration yields higher accuracy and related metrics than standard optimizers.

dimension_5_stated_limitations.text: The authors acknowledge that their approach is limited by focusing primarily on URL-based information, explicitly noting that it does not fully incorporate other informative aspects of phishing such as visual similarity of web content and user interaction behavior. They also concede a methodological limitation on the quantum side: no real quantum simulation or execution was carried out in their experimental setup, meaning all quantum components were evaluated only via classical simulation rather than on actual quantum hardware.

dimension_6_future_work.text: For practical deployment, the authors suggest that their findings could be used to develop security plugins for clients, browsers, and instant messaging applications running on endpoints such as PCs and smartphones, implying future engineering work to embed the model at network edges and personal terminals.

dimension_7_novelty_claim.text: The paper positions its main contribution as a dual-phase deep learning framework (pre-deployment and post-deployment) featuring a novel OptSHQCNN pipeline that integrates advanced preprocessing, attention-based feature extraction, meta-heuristic feature selection, a shallow hybrid quantum-classical CNN classifier, and optimizer-driven hyperparameter tuning. Within this pipeline, the SHQCNN is presented as a state-of-the-art hybrid architecture that leverages both classical and quantum computing principles, complemented by CBAM for focusing on important URL and code regions, RKOA for feature selection, SSOA for hyperparameter tuning, and OptBERT for URL encoding in the deployment phase.

dimension_8_methodological_notes.text: Methodologically, the work uses a two-phase (pre-deployment/post-deployment) pipeline with substantial preprocessing, including cleaning invalid and irrelevant features (removal of 19 attributes), handling missing values, and addressing class imbalance via SPE-ACGAN, as well as an explicitly defined feature-selection fitness function to combine multiple objectives. Feature extraction relies on CBAM to focus on crucial URL and webpage-code elements, with RKOA used as a meta-heuristic feature selector inspired by red kite social behavior, and SSOA performing hyperparameter tuning over a clearly specified search space (filters, batch sizes, dropout rates, kernel sizes). The post-deployment phase employs BERT-based URL encoding to capture contextual semantics, a RESTful server-side workflow for detection, and a concrete rule that missing external features are imputed with a default value of -1; experiments use multiple named public datasets with an 80/20 train-test split and an ablation study indicating that adding more processing stages monotonically improves accuracy.
